From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: John Patel <john.patel@healthcarecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC deployment - post-call recap

Hi John / Sofia 

Thanks for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key business drivers you shared:
- Data residency & regulatory: HealthcareCorp needs PHI to remain in your AWS accounts and meet HIPAA audit controls.
- Air-gapped / limited egress use-case: Certain workloads need to run in a highly restricted VPC with no internet egress.
- Low-latency inference for clinician-facing features (sub-100ms target for short prompts).
- Cost predictability for production rollout across three regions (US-East, US-West, EU planned).

Technical constraints we captured:
- No direct public endpoints allowed; all connections must be via VPC peering or Transit Gateway.
- Allowed outbound connections are limited to a small list (TLS to specific IPs/ports) - NetOps will provide firewall rules.
- KMS/HSM integration required for key management and customer-managed keys.
- Audit logs and request-level tracing must be retained for 365 days and accessible for SOC2 audits.

Proposed solution overview (Redwood Private - VPC deployment):
- Deploy Redwood control plane components to run in your VPC (customer-managed VPC with PrivateLink/TGW routing).
- Option for fully air-gapped inference nodes (no egress) for PHI workloads; model artifacts loaded via approved transfer process.
- Customer-managed KMS integration and log forwarding to your CloudWatch/S3 for retention.
- Latency tuning: dedicated GPU pool with optimized batching for clinician flows to meet the 100ms target.

Open questions / items we need from HealthcareCorp:
1) NetOps network diagram and CIDR ranges (attachment: network-diagram.png is an example schematic) - due 7/20
2) Firewall allowed IP/port list for outbound connections (we'll provide a minimal set) - due 7/20
3) SOC2 report and any additional compliance docs we should review (you mentioned SOC2 Type II): please share - due 7/21
4) Expected monthly inference QPS and peak concurrency for the pilot (helps size dedicated capacity)

Next steps / owners:
- Camila (Redwood): schedule architecture call with your NetOps + Security teams (propose 7/21 or 7/22).
- John (HealthcareCorp): share network diagram + firewall rules + expected pilot QPS by 7/20.
- Marissa (Redwood Solutions): prepare initial mutual action plan and draft SLA/contract redlines (see attached redwood-sla-draft.docx).
- Michael (Redwood Infra): prep sizing estimate + quantization/latency notes for the clinician flow.

Attachments included: network-diagram.png, SOC2-summary.pdf (Redwood SOC2 summary), redwood-sla-draft.docx

Thanks - happy to jump on another 30m to walk the plan.

Best,
Camila Reyes
